messages:
Zoe: Pulled together notes from the customer playthroughs — recurring theme: visual language in the Routing editor suggests rules are live when theyre just saved as drafts. Also a couple accessibility and simulator usability asks. Short list below.
Ravi: good call  list the specifics and well scope.
Zoe: 1) Saved state: green check feels like "applied". Customers expect green = live. 2) Drafts vs deployed: no clear distinction in the UI. 3) Simulator popover disappears too easily and hides long-match details. 4) Keyboard-only users cant re-order efficiently. 5) Validation messages are blunt and not prescriptive.
Lina: For saved state we could swap the color to a neutral grey + label: "Saved (staged)" and add a small help tooltip: "Draft saved locally; deploy to apply rules." That should reduce mistaken assumptions.
Omar: I'd rather keep the green for success but change the messaging: small badge says "Saved  (not live)" and add a subtle pulsing "deploy" CTA to guide users. We need to be careful with color semantics in docs though.
Jules: Accessibility note: don't rely on color alone. Add explicit text and an aria-label like "Saved in drafts; not applied". Also ensure the badge is announced when state changes.
Ravi: Simulator: make it sticky until explicit close or ESC. Add a "pin" icon so users can lock it while inspecting multiple rules. Also, expand the popover to show full match context with vertical scroll instead of truncating to a single line.
Zoe: On truncation parity: runtime trims by tokenized length; our preview truncates by chars which created a false-negative in a customer test. Short-term microcopy under the preview: "Preview may differ from runtime for very long inputs." Long-term option: call runtime preview or reuse tokenizer library.
Lina: Keyboard reordering: proposal: when a row has focus, support Ctrl/Cmd+Up and Ctrl/Cmd+Down to move. Also expose a small context menu item "Move" with arrow controls for screen-reader users. Add a visible hint on focus: "Move: Ctrl+↑ / Ctrl+↓".
Omar: Validation messages need to be actionable. Current: "invalid priority" -> change to: "Priority collision  two rules share the same priority. Pick a different priority or run Auto-resolve." Add an inline Auto-resolve CTA that shows a deterministic renumbering preview and an Undo toast.
Jules: For screen readers: - Mark the rule list role="list" and each row role="listitem". - Reorder control should have aria-roledescription="reorder handle" and aria-keyshortcuts="Ctrl+Up Ctrl+Down". - Simulator results container should be aria-live="polite" and aria-atomic="true"; when pinned, set role="dialog" and trap focus.
Ravi: Small UX question: should list order be the single source of truth or should numbers override? Customers are split. I suggest list order = default, numeric precedence editable in an "Edit precedence" mode. That avoids accidental direct edits and keeps the UI simple.
Zoe: Agree. Provide an "Edit precedence" toggle; when on, numbers become editable and a confirmation CTA appears. When off, show a tooltip: "Order determines routing. Toggle to edit precedence."
Lina: I'll mock two comps: default (drag primary) and edit-precedence mode (numbers editable + confirm/undo). Also include keyboard focus states and the pinned simulator. Can we review tomorrow 11am?
Ravi: Yes. I'll file a ticket for tokenizer parity as a dependency and a short-lived microcopy patch for the preview. Also add an RFC for keyboard shortcuts to avoid conflicts.
designbot: Created UX-5230: "Routing editor  visual language, simulator stickiness, keyboard reorder, and collision-driven auto-resolve"  assignees: Lina, Ravi; priority: Medium; due: 2024-07-15.
Zoe: Thanks all. Lina Ill upload the test video and annotated screenshots. Please include both the neutral badge and muted-green variants in the comps so we can run a quick preference test.
Jules: I'll run NVDA and VoiceOver checks on the comps once uploaded. Also will validate the announce strings for save state and Auto-resolve.
Ravi: Great. I'll split UX-5230 into smaller tickets for the sprint and link tokenizer parity. Follow-up in the RFC thread later today.
